config.theme: Go/no-go for the Aurora mobile app launch
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Go/no-go for the Aurora mobile app launch

personas.name: Maya
personas.goals: Get a firm launch date today
personas.hidden_agenda: Already hinted June 3rd to the exec team

personas.name: Raj
personas.goals: Do not ship with known stability issues
personas.hidden_agenda: Wants one more week to land the sync refactor

personas.name: Lena
personas.goals: Make sure the P1 bugs are tracked to closure
personas.hidden_agenda: Tired of being the last line of defence

personas.name: Tom
personas.hidden_agenda: Already booked a press slot and hasn't told anyone

agenda.title: Release readiness metrics
agenda.goal: Check stability and performance against the launch bar

agenda.title: Launch date
agenda.goal: Make the go/no-go call and pick a date

agenda.title: Launch comms and support
agenda.goal: Agree the announcement and support readiness

facts.statement: p95 cold start on the release candidate = 1.8 seconds
Typical app store review time = 2 days
Last major release shipped on April 22

beats.summary: Stability and performance against the bar; Tom misremembers the crash rate
Screenshots and copy are behind; legal review timing is fuzzy
The real fight: June 3rd vs one more week; a drift into Tom's marathon
Announcement, support readiness and budget; one question never gets answered

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Okay, so, thanks everyone. Four things today and I really want to land a date by the end, so let's keep moving.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Love it. I've got a hard stop at the top of the hour, just so you know.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Noted. First up, readiness. Raj, Lena, where are we on stability?

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: Honestly, better than I expected two weeks ago. The sync fix helped a lot.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Yeah, crash-free was like ninety-seven percent last week. That's basically perfect.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: Hm, that's not the number I have—

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: It was ninety-nine point two, Tom. Ninety-seven would actually be a disaster.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Oh. Okay, even better then.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: And the bar we agreed for launch was ninety-nine flat, right?

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: Right, ninety-nine. So we're over it, but not by a mile.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: To be fair, last week was a quiet week. Usage was down because of the holiday.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: So you think the number flatters us?

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: A little. I'd want to see it hold with normal traffic before I get excited.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: The thing is, it's never going to be a normal week, there's always something.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: For the record, the crash clusters we do have are almost all on older Android devices.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: How much of the beta is Android these days?

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: About sixty-two percent of active testers.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Which makes sense, that's our market.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: Cold start is the other thing. p95 cold start on the release candidate is one point eight seconds.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Is that good or bad? I genuinely don't remember what we were aiming for.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: It's fine. It's not great, but it's fine. Users won't notice on anything from the last three years.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: Older phones they will, though.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Older phones are slow at everything. Nobody blames the app for that.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: People absolutely blame the app for that. Read the store reviews sometime.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Okay. And the P1s? How many are still open?

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: Three. Two are on the sync screen and one is the login loop on tablets.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: The login loop is nasty. That one I don't want to ship with.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Is anyone actually on it right now?

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: Dmitri was looking at it on Friday, but he got pulled onto the payments thing.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: Which is how it always goes.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: Fine. I'll pair with Dmitri on the tablet login loop tomorrow morning and get a fix into the next build.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Great, thank you.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: And someone should probably keep an eye on the other two sync ones at some point.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Do we have any data on how many people actually hit the login thing?

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: Anyway, the sync ones are lower risk, they only show up when you're offline for days.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Okay. Overall, it sounds like the metrics are basically there, with the tablet bug as the open risk.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: That's fair. I'd say metrics are a soft yes, for now.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Let's move to the store listing. Tom, how are the assets looking?

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Screenshots are mostly done. The copy is done, it's great, I'm really happy with it.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: Are the screenshots from the release candidate or the old build?

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Mix. The onboarding ones are from the old build, which, yeah, I know.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: The onboarding flow changed quite a bit, so those will look wrong.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: It's three screens, it's not a big deal to redo them.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Who's redoing them, though? Design is slammed this week.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: I'll grab the new onboarding screenshots from the RC myself and get them to design by Wednesday.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Perfect.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: Has legal looked at the copy yet? There's the line about "clinically proven" that worried me.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: That line is staying, it tested really well.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Tom, that's not really what she asked.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Right, sorry. No, legal hasn't seen it yet. It's going over this week.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: Legal usually takes two weeks on anything health-related.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: I thought it was faster than that these days.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: It's five business days, that's what they told us after the last release.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Five days is fine. That still works.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Okay, but it has to actually go to them first.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: Maybe we drop the clinically proven line to be safe?

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Let's not decide that without seeing what legal says.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Yeah, let's see what legal says first and come back to it.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: And store review on top of that is usually a couple of days.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Two days, yeah, Apple's been quick lately.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: Side note, has anyone else noticed the coffee machine on four is broken again?

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: Since Monday. It's a tragedy.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: So legal plus store review is a fair bit of runway, minimum.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: Before anything else goes wrong, yes.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Okay, which brings us to the date. I'd love to land on June 3rd.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: I figured you'd say that.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: June 3rd is great for us. It lines up with the newsletter.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: Honestly, I'd rather go on the tenth. One more week lets the sync refactor land properly.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: We should really get the refactor reviewed by someone outside the team, whatever the date.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: What does the refactor give us that users would actually notice?

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: Fewer of those offline sync crashes, mostly. It's the stuff that hits the long-tail devices.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: Which is where most of our crashes are.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Can we ship the refactor in a point release after?

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: We could. It's just riskier to ship the big change after everyone's already on 2.0.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: How many people are in the beta now?

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Something like six thousand. It's been growing like crazy.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: It's forty-two hundred active. Six thousand is total sign-ups.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Active, sign-ups, whatever, it's a lot of people.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: And they're happy? What did the beta NPS land at?

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Fifty-one, which for health apps is honestly amazing.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: For the record, it was forty-one in the last survey.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Huh. I could swear I saw a higher number somewhere.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: Maybe that was the iOS-only cut.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Either way, it's decent. Okay. Tom, unrelated, but how was the marathon?

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Oh, brutal. Near the end I genuinely thought I was going to die.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: Did you finish under four hours in the end?

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Just over. So close. My knees are still not speaking to me.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: Okay, back to the date. Where does that leave us?

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Right. So the honest version is June 3rd with the refactor as a fast follow, or the tenth with it in.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: The thing is, I've sort of already got a press slot on the third.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: You've what?

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: It's soft! It's a soft hold. It can move, probably.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: That's the first I'm hearing of this.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: Same.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Okay. Let's not make the press slot the reason we pick a date.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: Agreed.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Here's where I am. Tablet login fix is a must, refactor is a nice-to-have.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: I can live with that, as long as the login loop is fixed and verified.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: Verified by QA, not just merged.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Fine. Then we're going with June 3rd, conditional on the tablet login fix passing QA by the twenty-eighth. That's the call.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Love it.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: Okay. Then the refactor is the one thing still hanging.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: Just to check, if the login fix slips, the date slips too?

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Yes. If it slips, we move to the tenth. No debate.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Can I tell the press contact it's the third, then?

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: You can tell them it's likely, not final.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: I'll write up the QA sign-off criteria for the login fix today so there's no argument later.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: Good. And the refactor ships in 2.0.1, not 2.0. That's decided.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Last item, comms and support. Tom, the announcement.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Blog post, newsletter, and the in-app banner on launch day. Plus paid social for two weeks.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: What's the paid social spend?

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: We've got a hundred and twenty grand for the whole launch.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: I have eighty-five thousand in the plan, not a hundred and twenty.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Eighty-five was before the press stuff.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: There is no "before the press stuff", the budget is the budget.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: Is support ready for a spike? Last launch they got hammered.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: They've trained fourteen agents on 2.0 so far.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: Fourteen is fewer than last time.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: Last time we shipped on April twenty-second and support was underwater for a week.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Maybe we keep a couple of engineers on support rotation for launch week.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: Maybe. I'd want to think about who, honestly.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: We could also just put a really good FAQ up.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: An FAQ doesn't answer the phone.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Who on the support side is actually signing off that they're ready?

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Anyway, I'll draft the launch blog post and send it round by Friday.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: Send it to me as well, I want to check the technical claims.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Sure, sure.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: Someone should probably update the release notes template too, it still says 1.9.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Okay. Should we do a dry run of the launch day checklist?

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: Probably worth it, the last one caught two things.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Let's maybe do the dry run next Thursday, if people are around.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: I'm around Thursday.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: I might be at the vendor thing, I'll know Monday.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Okay. I think that's everything. Recap is in the doc. Thanks all.

turns.speaker: Raj
turns.text: Thanks.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Thanks, team. Big launch!

timeline.text: Fourteen is fewer than last time.

timeline.speaker: Raj
timeline.text: Last time we shipped on April twenty-second and support was underwater for a week.

timeline.speaker: Maya
timeline.text: Maybe we keep a couple of engineers on support rotation for launch week.

timeline.speaker: Raj
timeline.text: Maybe. I'd want to think about who, honestly.

timeline.speaker: Tom
timeline.text: We could also just put a really good FAQ up.

timeline.speaker: Lena
timeline.text: An FAQ doesn't answer the phone.

timeline.speaker: Maya
timeline.text: Who on the support side is actually signing off that they're ready?

timeline.speaker: Tom
timeline.text: Anyway, I'll draft the launch blog post and send it round by Friday.

timeline.speaker: Raj
timeline.text: Send it to me as well, I want to check the technical claims.

timeline.speaker: Tom
timeline.text: Sure, sure.

timeline.speaker: Lena
timeline.text: Someone should probably update the release notes template too, it still says 1.9.

timeline.speaker: Maya
timeline.text: Okay. Should we do a dry run of the launch day checklist?

timeline.speaker: Raj
timeline.text: Probably worth it, the last one caught two things.

timeline.speaker: Maya
timeline.text: Let's maybe do the dry run next Thursday, if people are around.

timeline.speaker: Tom
timeline.text: I'm around Thursday.

timeline.speaker: Lena
timeline.text: I might be at the vendor thing, I'll know Monday.

timeline.speaker: Maya
timeline.text: Okay. I think that's everything. Recap is in the doc. Thanks all.

timeline.speaker: Raj
timeline.text: Thanks.

timeline.speaker: Tom
timeline.text: Thanks, team. Big launch!
